calls.prompt:
Create ONE new transparent game-map sprite of a modest Tang-era Chinese mountain-pass fortification. These two images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: reference 1 supplies the relaxed, irregular pen drawing and simple flat washes; reference 2 supplies the pale beige stone, quiet grey-brown roof and the Chinese architecture. Do not copy their layout, text, or watermark.
The gatehouse and a short standing curtain wall form ONE coherent building, in an elevated oblique view from SOUTHWEST looking NORTHEAST. The wall follows north-south: on the page it runs from lower-left foreground to upper-right background, close to vertical. The traffic passage runs east-west across that wall. Show exactly ONE readable arched entrance on the WEST-facing LEFT side of the gatehouse; the opposite east portal is hidden behind the solid building. The south-facing end face has NO arch. Do not try to show opposite facades simultaneously. Both the narrow wall top and a clear upright stone face must be visible, with wall feet touching the same ground plane. Short wall behind the tower to the north; a slightly longer wall in front toward the south, with uneven low stone ends.
Small restrained timber pavilion above a simple stone gateway, one understated grey-brown tiled roof; structure believable and sound, but drawing casual: irregular broken dark brown outlines, quick uneven roof strokes with gaps, sparse masonry marks, asymmetry in handwork, no meticulously drawn grids of bricks or tiles. Flat pale warm cream wash with a few light shadows. No saturated orange, metallic detail, glossy lighting, smooth digital gradients, giant palace, multiple towers, rigid isometric game-icon polish. It should feel like a small element cut from the illustrated reference, not a presentation render. No road, land patch, mountain, trees, river, labels or frame. Generous genuinely transparent margin all around; all architectural parts complete. Transparent PNG.

Create ONE very small Chinese Tang dynasty pass gatehouse map sprite on transparent background. Use first reference only for loose uneven ink strokes and second for Chinese architecture and pale palette. STRUCTURE FIRST: a solid short rectangular stone gatehouse base, one broad arch opening in its LEFT visible wall, the RIGHT visible wall is plain solid stone with NO door. The broad arch face points west/left on the map. Camera looking down slightly from the southwest, all verticals upright. North-south dimension of this compact building is SHORT, the arch front is clearly the long facade. On top one low simple timber watch pavilion with a gray-brown tiled hip roof. A few irregular strokes for tiles, sparse broken strokes for stone. Pale cream stone, muted warm gray roof, faded olive touches. This is a tiny historical map drawing, hand-penned rather than a meticulous architectural render. Outer contour subtly wobbly; geometry correct, restrained detail, no dark shading. IMPORTANT: standalone gatehouse ONLY, absolutely no attached side walls, no walls in front of the entrance, no extending curtain walls, no ground patch, no road, no people, no vegetation, no additional assets. Door arch clear and unobstructed to the left. Leave both solid end sides accessible for later separate wall segments, but draw no segments here. Do not make a long corridor or elaborate castle. Roof physically sits on walls, continuous support, no floating pieces. Transparent canvas.

Create a TRANSPARENT PNG atlas containing exactly FOUR clearly separated low, irregular woodland-edge clumps in a 2 by 2 grid, one clump per quadrant, with broad empty transparent gutters and margins. They are reusable tiny landscape sprites for a Chinese hand-drawn historical map. Match the first reference's spontaneously wobbly black pen outlines and flat pale washed colors, and the second reference's Chinese map style. Each clump should contain 9–15 overlapping varied trees with mostly rounded lumpy canopies; a few taller crooked slender trees and one sparse branching pine among them. Four genuinely DIFFERENT silhouette shapes and internal arrangements: first low broad scalloped band, second triangular staggered edge, third loose small crescent grove, fourth broken irregular wedge with gaps. No repeated identical tree shape, no ordered rows, no exact mirrored branches, no meticulous leaf detail. Trees aggregate into coherent woods, occasional visible crooked trunk, ink loosely suggestive. Muted pale sage and faded olive green, cream highlights, soft subdued blue-gray shade, NOT dark green or brown. No grass carpet, no ground oval or rectangular base, no land/water/mountains/buildings/text/shadows outside trees. Transparent canvas stays completely empty between clumps. Treat them as sketchy foliage silhouettes seen obliquely from above in an illustrated map, not isometric game sprites. Each clump much wider than tall. Composition fills each quadrant with generous empty border so no tree touches tile edges.

Draw a single short UPRIGHT STONE CURTAIN WALL segment for a tiny hand-drawn Chinese historical map. Transparent background, isolated wall only, no gate, no towers, no building, no landscape. Match rough loose uneven ink outlines and very pale warm cream flat wash of reference1 and delicate Chinese map look of reference2. Geometry critical: wall extends ALMOST VERTICALLY in the image from upper-left BACK end to lower-right FRONT end. Long axis slopes only 15 degrees from image vertical, total segment ground length about 120 px, wall height about 60 px, wall thickness about 14 px. Camera sees a substantial UPRIGHT WESTERN wall face on the LEFT of the thin top walkway. The upright face is visible through the entire length, from battlement TOP down to irregular wall FOOT. The lower/front end has a small rectangular plain stone end face. Walkway is narrow, viewed obliquely, NOT a broad ladder lying on the ground. About five or six crenellations, irregular hand-drawn stone cracks sparsely suggested, no brick grid, do not make military gray or yellow-orange. No mirror symmetry, no polished render, no cast shadow, no ground patch or rubble carpet. This is a simple short WALL MODULE with believable vertical volume, not ruins. Entire object well inside transparent margins. Keep architecture straight and supported, loose pen strokes not crooked structure.
